Timeline::defined¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

bool Timeline::defined() const noexcept

What It Tells You¶

defined() answers whether the Timeline owns a valid temporal payload. It is a state query, not an emptiness test and not an absent-instant test.

A defined timeline may be scalar, empty, or contain NaT. Those are all valid payload states. Use numel() to ask how many positions exist and isnat() to identify positions whose instant is absent.

Public factories return defined timelines or throw when construction fails, so ordinary application code rarely needs to poll this method after every factory call. It remains useful at API boundaries and in generic code that may receive moved-from or conditionally initialized objects.

Returns¶

true when the object has a valid backing payload; otherwise false. The method does not allocate, inspect timestamp values, or perform timezone work.

Examples¶

Example 1. Successful construction produces a defined object regardless of rank.

auto scalar = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:30:00Z");
auto vector = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-02-29T12:30:00Z",
    "2024-03-01T00:00:00Z",
});

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "scalar defined=" << scalar.defined() << "\n"
          << "vector defined=" << vector.defined() << "\n";

Output¶

scalar defined=true
vector defined=true

Example 2. NaT is data inside a defined timeline; it does not make the container undefined.

auto times = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2024-02-29T12:30:00Z",
    "",
});

std::cout << std::boolalpha
          << "defined=" << times.defined()
          << ", positions=" << times.numel() << "\n";
pluss::series::print(std::cout, times.isnat());
std::cout << "\n";

Output¶

defined=true, positions=2
Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=bool, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[false, true]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Do not use defined() to detect an empty timeline. A defined shape [0] has numel() == 0.

  • Do not use it to detect NaT. Absent instants are valid stored values.

  • A parse or shape error throws during construction; it does not normally return a public undefined sentinel for later inspection.

Summary¶

defined() validates the object state. numel() validates cardinality, and isnat() validates timestamp values; the three questions are deliberately separate.
